title: Speech by the Guest of Honor, Hon. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (MP), Minister for Investment, Industry, and Trade, at the opening of the National Conference on Commemoration of World Anti-Counterfeit Day, Mabele Hall, Dodoma, June 13
title_sw: HOTUBA YA MGENI RASMI, WAZIRI WA UWEKEZAJI, VIWANDA NA BIASHARA, MHE. DKT. ASHATU K. KIJAJI (Mb), AKIFUNGUA KONGAMANO LA KILELE CHA MAADHIMISHO YA KITAIFA YA SIKU YA KUDHIBITI BIDHAA BANDIA DUNIANI, UKUMBI WA MABELE, DODOMA, JUNI 13, 2023
text:
HOTUBA YA MGENI RASMI, WAZIRI WA UWEKEZAJI, VIWANDA NA
BIASHARA, MHE. DKT. ASHATU K. KIJAJI (Mb), AKIFUNGUA
KONGAMANO LA KILELE CHA MAADHIMISHO YA KITAIFA YA SIKU YA
KUDHIBITI BIDHAA BANDIA DUNIANI, UKUMBI WA MABELE, DODOMA,
JUNI 13, 2023
Mheshimiwa Rosemary Sinyamule, Mkuu wa Mkoa wa Dodoma,
Mheshimiwa Dkt. Hashil Abdallah, Katibu Mkuu, Wizara ya Uwekezaji,
Viwanda na Biashara,
Wadau wa Maendeleo,
Waheshimiwa Wabunge ambao ni Wajumbe wa Kamati ya Kudumu ya Bunge
ya Viwanda, Biashara, Kilimo na Mifugo,
Dkt. Aggrey Mlimuka, Mwenyekiti wa Tume ya Ushindani (FCC),
Wajumbe wa Tume ya Ushindani (FCC),
Ndg. William Erio, Mkaguzi Mkuu wa Sheria ya Alama za Bidhaa ambaye pia
ni Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Tume ya Ushindani (FCC),
Ndg. Mohammed Sijamini Mohammed, Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Tume ya
Ushindani Halali wa Biashara Zanzibar (ZFCC),
Wamiliki wa Alama za Bidhaa pamoja na Wawakilishi wa Vyama na
Wafanyabiashara,
Wawakilishi kutoka Wizara, Taasisi, Idara za Serikali na Mamlaka za Tawala za
Mikoa na Wilaya,
Wawakilishi kutoka Taasisi za Ushauri wa Kisheria na Vyama vya Uwakilishi
wa Watumiaji,
1

Menejimenti na Wafanyakazi wa FCC,
Waandishi wa Habari,
Mabibi na Mabwana
Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania!
Awali ya yote napenda kutumia fursa hii kumshukuru Mwenyezi Mungu mwingi wa
rehema kwa kutuamsha salama tukiwa na afya njema na kutuwezesha kushiriki
katika maadhimisho haya adhimu. Napenda pia kuushukuru uongozi wa Tume ya
Ushindani (FCC) kwa kunialika kuwa mgeni rasmi katika maadhimisho haya.
Aidha, nitumie fursa hii kuwashukuru wadau wote walioitikia wito wa kushiriki katika
maadhimisho haya muhimu wakiwemo uongozi wa Mkoa wa Dodoma chini ya
Mheshimiwa Mkuu wa Mkoa, Waheshimiwa Wajumbe wa Kamati ya Kudumu ya
Bunge ya Viwanda, Biashara, Kilimo na Mifugo wakiongozwa na Mheshimiwa
David Mwakiposa Khenzile (Mb), Wadau wa maendeleo, wamiliki wa Alama za
Biashara, vyama vya uwakilishi wa watumiaji na wanafunzi kutoka vyuo vya elimu
ya juu na wadau wote mliopo hapa kwa kutenga muda wenu na kuhudhuria
kongamano hili.
Pia nimefurahishwa kufahamu kuwa wawakilishi wa wafanyabiashara, wazalishaji,
wawakilishi kutoka chama cha Mawakala wa Ushuru wa Forodha, Vyombo vya
Serikali vya usimamizi wa soko na uwezeshaji kibiashara pamoja na wamiliki wa
Alama za Biashara ni miongoni mwa washiriki wa Kongamano hili ambalo
linaadhimishwa chini ya kauli mbiu “Kukuza Ubia Kati ya Sekta ya Umma na
Binafsi katika Kudhibiti Bidhaa Bandia”.
Waswahili wanasema mtu akikualika amekuheshimu, lakini akiitikia wito
amekuheshimu zaidi. Hivyo, tunapenda kuwashukuru kwa heshima hii mliyotupatia
ya kujumuika nasi.
2

Mwitikio wenu mkubwa wa mahudhurio katika kongamano hili la leo ni faraja katika
Wizara yangu, mkiakisi kwamba wadau wote mnakerwa na kuumizwa na biashara
ya bidhaa bandia. Hivyo, ni dhahiri kwamba mpo tayari kushirikiana na Serikali na
Taasisi yetu ya FCC katika mapambano dhidi ya bidhaa bandia kama inavyosema
kauli mbiu ya maadhimisho haya.
Wakati nilipopata mwaliko wa FCC wa kushiriki katika Maadhimisho haya, sikusita
hata kidogo kuitikia wito huo kwa kuwa suala hili la kupambana na bidhaa bandia ni
la muhimu sana katika kuhakikisha kuwa Wizara yangu ambayo inashughulikia
Uwekezaji, Viwanda na Biashara, inatekeleza majukumu yake kwa ufanisi.
Bidhaa Bandia zinaathiri uwekezaji kwa kuwa wawekezaji wanavutiwa zaidi
kuwekeza katika nchi zenye mifumo thabiti ya udhibiti (regulatory regimes)
zinazoonesha juhudi za wazi za kudhibiti bidhaa bandia, wakiamini kuwa uwekezaji
wao utalipa. Kama sote tunavyofahamu, kuvutia uwekezaji kutoka nje (Foreign
Direct Investment) ni muhimu sana katika kuleta maendeleo ya kiuchumi katika
nchi yoyote duniani, ikiwemo Tanzania. Ni Dhahiri basi kwamba udhibiti wa bidhaa
bandia ni kichocheo cha kuvutia wawekezaji zaidi hapa nchini, kama inavyoonesha
katika takwimu za Kituo cha Uwekezaji Nchini (TIC).
Wizara yangu pia inashughulika na viwanda vinavyozalisha bidhaa kwa nia ya
kuziuza ndani na nje ya mipaka yetu. Kudhibiti bidhaa bandia kwa ufanisi
kunaongeza soko la bidhaa zinazozalishwa katika viwanda na hivyo kuchochea
viwanda vilivyopo kuongeza uzalishaji na viwanda vipya kuanzishwa.
Kuongezeka kwa uzalishaji katika viwanda kutakuza ajira, kutaongeza mapato kwa
njia ya kodi na kuongeza urahisi wa upatikanaji wa bidhaa kwa bei nafuu
(affordable) kutokana na kuongezeka kwa ushindani katika soko.
3

Udhibiti mzuri wa biashara ya bidhaa bandia pia utasaidia kushamirisha biashara
ya kiushindani na itaiwezesha nchi yetu kutumia fursa za masoko ya kikanda, Soko
Huru la Afrika (AcFTA) na Masoko ya Kimataifa.
Katika kutekeleza haya ni dhahiri kwamba ushirikiano madhubuti na wa karibu wa
sekta binafsi na sekta ya Umma ni muhimu kuwepo kutokana na ukweli kwamba
wadau wa shughuli za uwekezaji, viwanda na biashara wanatoka katika sekta
binafsi na vyombo vya Serikali ndivyo vinavyotengeneza mazingira wezeshi katika
soko kwa utendaji wa ufanisi wa kibiashara ikiwemo udhibiti wa bidhaa bandia.
Serikali inapenda kuona kuwa udhibiti wa bidhaa bandia unafanyika kwa ufanisi
zaidi kwa juhudi za pamoja za wadau wote wa biashara.
Serikali inatambua na inapongeza juhudi za FCC katika kudhibiti bidhaa bandia.
Takwimu zinaonesha kuwa kiwango cha bidhaa bandia zinaoingia nchini ni kidogo.
Mathalan, katika miezi tisa ya kwanza ya mwaka wa fedha 2022/2023, FCC
ilikagua makasha ya kusafirishia mizigo (containers) 7918 katika Bandari ya Dar es
Salaam, ambapo kati ya hayo makasha 206 tu, sawa na asilimia 2.6, yalikutwa
yakiwa na shehena ya bidhaa zinazokiuka Sheria ya Alama za Bidhaa. Hii
inamaanisha kuwa asilimia 97.4 ya bidhaa zote zilizokaguliwa katika kipindi hicho,
zilikidhi matakwa ya Sheria ya Alama za Bidhaa na hivyo kuwa bidhaa halali.
Takwimu hizi zinaonesha wazi kuwa FCC kwa kushirikiana na vyombo vingine vya
Serikali na waagizaji na wazalishaji wa bidhaa mbalimbali wanafanya kazi nzuri na
kuifanya nchi yetu kuwa ni sehemu nzuri ya kuwekeza kwa nia ya kuzalisha bidhaa
mbalimbali, sehemu nzuri ya kufanya biashara na kujenga viwanda.
Pamoja na mafanikio haya, ni dhahiri kwamba kuongezeka kwa ushirikiano kati ya
FCC na wadau wake kutafanya udhibiti dhidi ya bidhaa bandia kuwa ya mafanikio
zaidi. Aina hizi za ushirikiano ni pamoja na:
4

1. kuongeza ushirikiano katika kutoa elimu kwa wadau kuhusu madhara ya
bidhaa bandia na jinsi ya kuzitambua,
2. Waagizaji wakubwa wakubwa wa bidhaa kutoingiza nchini bidhaa bandia;
3. Wakala wa Ushuru wa Forodha kutokukubali kusafirisha na kuingiza bidhaa
bandia;
4. Balozi za nchi ambazo bidhaa zake zinapita katika nchi ya Tanzania kwa
kushirikiana na mamlaka husika katika nchi zao kuwaelimisha
wafanyabiashara wao kutokuagiza na kupitisha bidhaa bandia nchini
Tanzania
5. Mashirika ya Kimataifa na Asasi mbalimbali za uwezeshaji wa kibiashara
kuisaidia FCC katika kupata mafunzo na nyenzo za kisasa za kutambua na
kudhibiti bidhaa bandia;
6. Kuuelimisha Umma kuhusu madhara ya bidhaa bandia na hivyo kuwashauri
waepuke kuzinunua;
Serikali kwa upande wake, kupitia Wizara, itasimamia ukamilishaji wa maboresho
ya Sheria ya Alama za Bidhaa katika kuunga mkono juhudi hizo na kuleta ufanisi
zaidi kiutendaji.
Natambua kuwa FCC kwa muda mrefu ilikuwa imejikita zaidi katika kaguzi kwenye
bandari ya Dar es Salaam pamoja na bandari zake kavu zipatazo 15. Eneo la
ukaguzi kwa sasa linaongezeka ambapo kutakuwa na Bandari Kavu ya Kwala,
Mkoani Pwani, pamoja na vituo vya ukaguzi wa pamoja mipakani (OSBPs)
vilivyojengwa na vinavyoendelea kujengwa kwa uratibu wa Jumuiya ya Afrika
Mashariki kupitia Mradi wa Uboreshaji wa Biashara na Usafirishaji (East African
Trade and Transport Facilitation Project -EATTFP), kwa ufadhili wa Taasisi ya
TradeMark East Africa (TMEA), Benki ya Maendeleo ya Afrika (AfDB), Benki ya
Dunia na Shirika la Maendeleo la Ushirikiano la Japan (JICA).
5

Kwakuwa FCC imeshaanzisha ofisi za Kanda katika Miji ya Mwanza, Arusha na
Mbeya, naielekeza iongeze juhudi katika kufanya kaguzi za bidhaa bandia katika
maeneo ya mipakani na Kanda hizo. Serikali inakaribisha uungwaji mkono wa
wadau katika kuiwezesha FCC katika kufanikisha utendaji wa ofisi hizo kwa ufanisi.
Ndugu Washiriki
Kwa mujibu wa ratiba ya kongamano la leo, mada mbalimbali zitawasilishwa na
kujadiliwa. Ni matumaini yangu kuwa zitakuwa zinajadiliwa kwa kina na kutolewa
mapendekezo ya namna bora ya kuboresha uhusiano kati ya sekta ya Umma na
binafsi katika kudhibiti bidhaa bandia katika maeneo yaliyoainishwa kwenye mada
na maeneo mengine kwa ujumla.
Baada ya kusema hayo nawatakiwa mkutano mwema
Sasa ninayo furaha kutamka kuwa Kongamano hili la Kilele cha Maadhimisho ya
Kitaifa ya Siku ya Udhibiti wa Bidhaa Duniani, limefunguliwa rasmi.
Asanteni kwa kunisikiliza.
Mhe. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (Mb)
Waziri wa Uwekezaji, Viwanda na Biashara
Dodoma, Juni 13, 2023
Speech by the Guest of Honor, Hon. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (MP), Minister for
Investment, Industry, and Trade, at the opening of the National Conference on
Commemoration of World Anti-Counterfeit Day, Mabele Hall, Dodoma, June 13,
2023.
6

Honorable Rosemary Sinyamule, Dodoma Regional Commissioner,
Honorable Dr. Hashil Abdallah, Permanent Secretary, Ministry for Industry and
Trade,
Development Partners,
Honorable Members of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry, Trade,
Agriculture, and Livestock,
Dr. Aggrey Mlimuka, Chairperson of the Fair Competition Commission (FCC),
Members of the Commission (FCC),
Mr. William Erio, Chief Inspector of Trademarks, who also serves as the Director-
General of the Fair Competition Commission (FCC),
Mr. Mohammed Sijamini Mohammed, Director General of ZFCC,
Brand Owners and Representatives of Associations and Traders,
Representatives from Ministries, Institutions, Government Departments, and
Regional and District Administrative Authorities,
Representatives from Legal Consultancy Institutions and Consumer Representation
Associations,
Management and Staff of the FCC,
Members of the Press,
Ladies and Gentlemen,
I would like to use this opportunity to thank the Almighty God for enabling us to
participate in these significant celebrations. I therefore, would like to express my
gratitude to the leadership of the Fair Competition Commission (FCC) for inviting
me to be the esteemed guest at these celebrations.
I extend my appreciation to all stakeholders who responded to the call to participate
in these important celebrations, including the Dodoma Regional leadership under
the Regional Commissioner, members of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on
7

Industry, Trade, Agriculture, and Livestock led by Honorable David Mwakiposa
Khenzile (MP), development partners, Ambassadors from various countries, brand
owners, consumer representation associations, and students from higher education
institutions, among others, for taking the time to attend this conference.
I am also pleased to learn that representatives from traders, producers,
representatives from the Customs Agents Association, Government market
management and trade facilitation agencies, as well as brand owners, are among
the participants in this conference.
As the Swahili saying goes, when someone invites you, they respect you, but when
you respond to the invitation, you show even greater respect. Therefore, we thank
you for the value you have shown us by joining us.
Your significant response in attendance at this summit is a source of
encouragement for my ministry, reflecting that all stakeholders are concerned and
affected by the trade in counterfeit goods. It is clear that you are ready to
collaborate with the government and FCC in the fight against counterfeit goods, as
emphasized by the theme of these celebrations.
When I received the FCC's invitation to participate in these celebrations, I did not
hesitate at all to respond to that call because the issue of combating counterfeit
goods is crucial in ensuring that my ministry, which deals with Industry and Trade,
performs its duties efficiently.
Counterfeit goods affect Industry, Trade and investment as well because investors
are more attracted to invest in countries with robust regulatory regimes that show
clear efforts to control counterfeit goods, believing that their investment will pay off.
As we all know, attracting foreign direct investment is crucial for economic
development in any country, including Tanzania. It is clear, therefore, that effective
control of counterfeit goods is a catalyst for attracting more investors to our country,
as reflected in the statistics from the Tanzania Investment Center (TIC).
8

My ministry is also responsible for industries that produce goods for sale within and
outside our borders. Effective control of counterfeit goods increases the market for
products manufactured in industries, thus stimulating existing industries to increase
production and new industries to be established.
Increased production in industries will create employment, increase revenue
through taxes, and make it easier for consumers to access affordable goods due to
increased competition in the market.
Effective control of the trade in counterfeit goods will also help promote competitive
trade and enable our country to take advantage of regional markets, the African
Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), and international markets.
In implementing these measures, it is evident that strong and close collaboration
between the private and public sectors is necessary, given that stakeholders in
investment, industry, and trade come from the private sector, and government
agencies create an enabling environment in the market for efficient business
performance, including the control of counterfeit goods.
The government is eager to see that the control of counterfeit goods is more
effective through joint efforts of all business stakeholders. The government
recognizes and applauds the efforts of the FCC in the fight against counterfeit
goods. Statistics show that the level of counterfeit goods entering the country is
minimal. For example, in the first nine months of the fiscal year 2022/2023, the FCC
inspected 7,918 cargo containers at the Dar es Salaam Port. Out of these, only 206
containers, equivalent to 2.6%, were found to contain goods violating the
Trademarks Act. This means that 97.4% of all inspected goods during that period
complied with the requirements of the Trademarks Act and were thus legitimate
products.
These statistics clearly show that the FCC, in collaboration with other government
agencies and importers and producers of various goods, is doing a commendable
job, making our country an attractive place to invest in and produce various
9

products. Despite these successes, it is evident that increased collaboration
between the FCC and its stakeholders will make the fight against counterfeit goods
even more successful. These types of collaborations include:
1. Increasing collaboration in educating stakeholders about the dangers or negative
impact of counterfeit goods and how to identify them.
2. Major importers refraining from importing counterfeit goods.
3. Customs Agents refusing to transport and import counterfeit goods.
4. Embassies of countries whose products pass through Tanzania collaborating
with relevant authorities in their countries to educate their traders not to import and
pass counterfeit goods in Tanzania.
5. International organizations and various business empowerment organizations
assist the FCC in obtaining modern training and tools to identify and control
counterfeit goods.
6. Educating the public about the dangers and negativity of counterfeit goods,
advising them to avoid buying them.
The government, on its part, through the Ministry, will oversee the completion of
improvements to the TradeMarks Act to support these efforts and bring about more
operational efficiency.
I acknowledge that the FCC has long focused more on inspections at the Dar es
Salaam port and its 15 dry ports. The inspection area is expanding, and there will
be the Kwala Dry Port in Pwani Region, as well as Joint Border Post inspection
points (OSBPs) that are being built and continue to be constructed under the
coordination of the East African Community through the East African Trade and
Transport Facilitation Project (EATTFP), funded by TradeMark East Africa (TMEA),
the African Development Bank (AfDB), the World Bank, and the Japan International
Cooperation Agency (JICA).
As the FCC has already established Zonal Offices in Mwanza, Arusha, and Mbeya,
I direct it to increase efforts in inspecting counterfeit goods at border areas and
10

those regions. The government welcomes and encourages the support of
stakeholders to enable the FCC to efficiently carry out its functions in these offices.
Dear participants, based on today's conference schedule, various topics will be
presented and discussed. I hope that they will be thoroughly discussed, and
recommendations on how to improve the relationship between the public and
private sectors in combating counterfeit goods in the specified areas and others will
be made.
Having said that, I wish you a fruitful moment.
Now, I am pleased to declare that this National Conference on the World Anti-
Counterfeit Day is officially open.
Thank you for listening.
Hon. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (MP)
Minister of Investment, Industry, and Trade
Dodoma, June 13, 2023
